![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `page.pdf()` method is only supported in Chromium headless mode. Since the browser is initialized with `headless: false` in `src/index.ts` (line 61) to facilitate user login, this tool will likely fail with an error when invoked. Consider using a separate headless browser context for PDF generation or documenting this limitation.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `waitForSelector` call ignores errors via `.catch(() => {})`. If the invoice content fails to load within the 5-second timeout (e.g., due to network issues or an unexpected page state), the function will proceed to generate a PDF of an incomplete or incorrect page. It is safer to handle the timeout and return an error result.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `outputPath` defaults to the `Downloads` directory, but Playwright's `page.pdf({ path })` will throw an error if the target directory does not exist. It is recommended to ensure the directory exists (e.g., using `fs.mkdirSync` with `{ recursive: true }`) before calling `downloadInvoice`.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Add validation for invalid date ranges.**

The date-window inference logic does not validate that `startDate ≤ endDate` or that dates are not in the future. This could lead to unexpected `timeFilter` selection (e.g., negative `daysAgo` values if `startDate` is in the future) and might confuse users.

Consider adding defensive checks at the start of the block:




<details>
<summary>🛡️ Suggested validation</summary>

```diff
 } else if (params.startDate) {
   const now = new Date();
   const start = params.startDate;
   const end = params.endDate ?? now;
+  
+  // Validate date range
+  if (start > end) {
+    throw new Error(`Invalid date range: startDate (${start.toISOString()}) must be <= endDate (${end.toISOString()})`);
+  }
+  if (start > now) {
+    throw new Error(`Invalid date range: startDate (${start.toISOString()}) cannot be in the future`);
+  }
+  
   const daysAgo = (d: Date) =>
     (now.getTime() - d.getTime()) / (1000 * 60 * 60 * 24);
```

</details>

Using the nullish coalescing operator (`??`) allows an empty string (`""`) to be used as the `BROWSER_DATA_DIR` if the environment variable `AMAZON_ORDERS_BROWSER_DATA_DIR` is defined but empty. This can cause Playwright's `launchPersistentContext` to fail or behave unexpectedly.
```suggestion
const BROWSER_DATA_DIR =
  process.env.AMAZON_ORDERS_BROWSER_DATA_DIR ||
  join(homedir(), ".amazon-order-history-mcp", "browser-data");
```

🌐 Web query:

`Playwright Locator.allTextContents documentation returns textContent raw whitespace Playwright 1.40`

💡 Result:

The Playwright method locator.allTextContents returns the raw text content of all matched elements, including all descendant elements [1]. This behavior directly reflects the underlying DOM node.textContent property [2][3][4]. As a result, the returned strings include all original whitespace, such as newlines, tabs, and extra spaces present in the HTML source [1][5]. Playwright does not perform any automatic trimming or normalization of whitespace for this specific method [1][5]. For Playwright 1.40 and other versions, if you require clean, whitespace-normalized strings, you must handle the formatting yourself using standard JavaScript string methods, such as.trim or regular expressions, when processing the returned array [1]. Example usage: const texts = await page.locator('.list-item').allTextContents; const cleanedTexts = texts.map(text => text.trim); Note that this behavior differs from Playwright's locator-based text matching methods (e.g., page.getByText), which do automatically normalize whitespace [2][6]. For testing assertions, Playwright documentation explicitly recommends using expect(locator).toHaveText instead of allTextContents to avoid potential flakiness and issues related to unexpected whitespace [2][3].

Citations:

- 1: https://runebook.dev/en/docs/playwright/api/class-locator/locator-all-text-contents
- 2: https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator
- 3: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/main/docs/src/api/class-locator.md
- 4: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/b820ebd7e3c3e55f05a80aa6aaf35cd10c085d37/packages/playwright-core/src/client/locator.ts
- 5: GitHub issue 11325 in microsoft/playwright (link omitted to avoid creating a cross-reference)
- 6: https://playwright.dev/docs/locators

---



</details>
